title: Cyberdeck — AI Terminal Build
summary: Build a custom steampunk cyberdeck with expressive LEDs, film the build, post the video. Future: sell DIY kits with OpenClaw pre-installed.

overview.what: A DIY portable computer built from a Raspberry Pi inside a rugged case with steampunk brass + green LED aesthetic. The deck expresses AI state through hardware — LEDs pulse when thinking, shift color when executing. Film the build as content.
overview.status_detail: Research phase complete. Reference images collected across 4 style categories (steampunk, green matrix, pelican classic, recent 2025-2026 builds). No parts ordered yet.

columns.name: Pick final aesthetic
values: Decide between steampunk brass vs green glow vs hybrid
Review reference pages in Cognition OS, pick top 3 builds to draw from

columns.name: Parts list + order
values: Spec out every component, find sources, order
Start with: Pi 5, screen size, keyboard, case type, LED strips

columns.name: Plan build video
values: Shot list, narrative arc, music choice
Watch top cyberdeck build videos for format inspiration

columns.name: Build + film
values: Actually build it and capture footage

considerations.label: Timing
considerations.detail: Cyberdecks are peaking NOW — Newsweek coverage, TikTok explosion. Window is open.

considerations.label: Unique angle
considerations.detail: Nobody is doing 'AI that lives in the machine' with expressive hardware. The skeleton key power-on alone is a clip.

considerations.label: Content > product
considerations.detail: The video is the primary deliverable. Kit business is secondary and only if demand is proven.

considerations.label: LED system
considerations.detail: Amber=thinking, blue=listening, green=executing, red=error. Could use NeoPixels controlled by Pi GPIO.

notes:
The build video narrative: 'I built an AI that lives in a steampunk machine.' Dark workshop, brass and green light, hands assembling it, first boot — the key turns, green light floods the case, terminal text starts scrolling.

Key reference builds:
- Hackaday steampunk contest winner (wood, leather, brass, e-paper)
- Jay Doscher Recovery Kit (the OG Pelican cyberdeck)
- Gundam cyberdeck (programmable LED storytelling — closest to our expressive hardware idea)
